cards.explanation: The answer is fury, friends. The verse says Jerusalem drank from the hand of the LORD "…the cup of His fury…" It also says she "…drained the goblet to the dregs…" That's a heavy cup, and she took it all the way down.

The answer is False. Jerusalem didn't stop at one sip, because the text says she "…drained the goblet to the dregs…" That's every last drop, down to the bottom. If I did that with a batch of dough, there'd be nothing left but crumbs and a very guilty mustache.

The answer is False, and it's a hard line to read. Isaiah says, "among all the sons she brought up, there is no one to take her hand." The same verse says, "Among all the sons she bore, there is no one to guide her…"

The answer is that they have fainted, friends. "Your sons have fainted; they lie at the head of every street, like an antelope in a net." Fainted is the word the verse uses. The antelope in a net is the picture the verse gives.
The answer is True, friends. The same verse says it: "They are full of the wrath of the LORD, the rebuke of your God." This is a heavy part. The text doesn't hurry past it, and I won't either.

The answer is that He removes it from her hand. That's the turn, friends. The LORD says, "See, I have removed from your hand the cup of staggering." The One speaking is the LORD who defends His people.

The answer is never. The LORD says, "From that goblet, the cup of My fury, you will never drink again." That comes right after He says, "See, I have removed from your hand the cup of staggering." It's a promise with no end date and no fine print.

The answer is her tormentors. The LORD says, "I will place it in the hands of your tormentors…" The cup leaves Jerusalem's hand and goes to the ones who tormented her. The verse describes them as the ones who told her to lie down so they could walk over her.
The answer is "Lie down, so we can walk over you…" It's a cruel thing to tell anyone. I think this one hurts, friends, and the LORD sees it too.

The answer is her garments of splendor. The prophet says, "Put on your garments of splendor, O Jerusalem, holy city!" Right before that he tells her to clothe herself with strength. Strength and splendor, both on together, and what a change of tone after the cup of fury.
The answer is False. The text says, "For the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer enter you." Jerusalem is called the holy city in the same verse. "No longer" is the passage's own wording.

The answer is her chains, friends. The prophet says, "Remove the chains from your neck, O captive Daughter of Zion." He tells her to take them off and rise, which is the whole point of the wake-up call.

The answer is without money. The LORD says, "You were sold for nothing, and without money you will be redeemed." She was sold for nothing, and she'll be redeemed without money. Nobody's pulling out a wallet in that sentence.

The answer is Egypt. The LORD says, "At first My people went down to Egypt to live, then Assyria oppressed them without cause." He's looking back over His people's story, one place at a time. Egypt comes first, then Assyria.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "Therefore My people will know My name; therefore they will know on that day that I am He who speaks." That's what His people will know on that day. And He ends with, "Here I am!"

The answer is True, friends. The prophet says, "How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news…" It's a pretty big compliment for a pair of feet. They're beautiful because of what the messenger is carrying.
The answer is "Your God reigns!" It comes right after those words about proclaiming peace and salvation. It's short, and that's the good news.

The answer is that the LORD returns to Zion. Isaiah says, "For every eye will see when the LORD returns to Zion." Just before that he says, "Listen! Your watchmen lift up their voices, together they shout for joy." That return is the reason for the shouting.
The answer is comforted, friends. The text says, "…the LORD has comforted His people; He has redeemed Jerusalem." Back in chapter 51, the question was who could comfort her, and here is the answer.

The answer is the salvation of our God. The verse says, "all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God." That comes after the LORD has bared His holy arm in the sight of all the nations. The ends of the earth are the ones named as seeing it.

The answer is those who carry the vessels of the LORD. The prophet says, "…purify yourselves, you who carry the vessels of the LORD." Right before that he calls out, "Depart, depart, go out from there!" He's speaking to the ones carrying the LORD's vessels, and he tells them to go out.
The answer is False. The text says, "…you will not leave in a hurry nor flee in haste…" The reason follows right behind it: "…for the LORD goes before you…"

The answer is the God of Israel, friends. The verse says, "…the LORD goes before you, and the God of Israel is your rear guard." He's out in front, and He's at the back too. Both ends of the line are covered.
